candidates.statement: Slack is the primary mode of communication within the university; the stakeholder mainly uses it to communicate with peers and professors.

evidence_candidates.quote: slack is the primary mode of communication within my university, so I mainly use Slack to communicate with my peers and my professors,

candidates.statement: Use Slack every day to talk to peers, teaching assistants in various subjects, and professors, with usage growing over the semester.

evidence_candidates.quote: it's definitely something that I use every day to talk to my peers, my teaching, teaching assistants in various subjects, and also my professors.

candidates.statement: Prefer Slack for instant communication with anyone in the university: knowing only a name or surname is enough to look a person up and reach out almost immediately, and it works from phone or laptop.
context: Person is a member of the university

evidence_candidates.quote: I prefer using slack because it's instant communication with anyone I wish to talk to within the university.
if I know their name, or sometimes even their last name, I can look them up, and I can reach out to them almost immediately.

candidates.statement: Enjoy being able to reach people both over the phone and when the laptop is open.

evidence_candidates.quote: And I can do it over my phone. I can do it if my laptop's open and I definitely enjoy that aspect, yeah,

candidates.statement: Use the channel feature to reach a wide audience immediately, which would take more time over email.

evidence_candidates.quote: I also like the channel feature within slack, where I can reach a wide audience immediately.

candidates.statement: Have the history of a channel available on joining, including information posted before joining.

evidence_candidates.quote: I have access to information that was there before I even joined the channel

candidates.statement: Know at any point what people are talking about and sharing, including what is happening in the department, the program, and around campus.
candidates.modality: stated value ("it's good to know", "I like to hear")

evidence_candidates.quote: I like to hear what's happening around within the department, within the program, what's happening around campus.

candidates.statement: Share documents with teammates when collaborating, as the most used direct-messaging feature.

evidence_candidates.quote: my most used feature is sharing documents when collaborating with teammates

candidates.statement: Sharing a document instantly with a teammate supports the first goal named, instant communication.

evidence_candidates.quote: slack provides a pretty neat way to share a document instantly with a teammate

candidates.statement: Attach any type of file when sharing a document, and format the accompanying message as wanted.

evidence_candidates.quote: there is an option to attach a document, and I can attach any type of file I want.

candidates.statement: Use the search feature with keywords to look for something specific, such as something a professor said in a past subject.

evidence_candidates.quote: there is a search feature that I would use to I would enter keywords to look, to look for something specific.

candidates.statement: When searching by keyword, results contain far too much information to sift through unless the exact target is already known, which makes finding the wanted message difficult.

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes when I search for a keyword or keywords, I get way too much information in the search results.
So it's a little difficult to pass through things unless I know exactly what I'm looking for.

candidates.statement: Video and audio calls are harder to start than in Microsoft Teams; it takes a little more time and several windows to navigate, and it would be easier with more direct access.

evidence_candidates.quote: I find that it's a little harder to have video calls or audio calls. I mean it, even though it's possible, it it takes a little more time.
it would be easier if it was just more access.

candidates.statement: As an alternative to Slack calls, call the person directly by phone or email when they are known well enough.
candidates.modality: personal workaround, comparative preference for speed
context: Email or phone number already held

evidence_candidates.quote: if I know the person well enough, do you know if I have their email with not their emails, or if their phone number with me, I would just call them.

candidates.statement: Keep using Slack rather than switch to another application, because it is the fastest way to communicate within the university and the limitations are not convincing enough to leave.

evidence_candidates.quote: I would still use Slack because ultimately, it's the fastest way to communicate with people within the university.
I don't think it's, it's convincing enough for me to switch to a different application

candidates.statement: Would like a quick email feature that immediately navigates to Outlook, Gmail or another standard email app to email a person, for situations where an email is expected such as formal communication with teaching assistants or professors.
candidates.modality: explicit request ("I would like", "would be super useful")

evidence_candidates.quote: I would like a quick email feature, because I feel like sometimes, again I'm comparing it to Microsoft Teams a little bit.
there are certain situations where you know an email is expected, like when you have formal communication within with your teaching assistants or your professors.

candidates.statement: Would like the call feature to be more accessible, especially in a group setting.

evidence_candidates.quote: And adding on to that, I would like the call feature more accessible as well, yeah, especially in a group setting

candidates.statement: Advise a new Slack user to be aware that everyone in the community is highly accessible through name or surname, and to highlight document-sharing and similar collaboration features.
candidates.modality: advice to third parties (hypothetical new user)

evidence_candidates.quote: everyone within this lac community is super accessible, that all you need to know is you know their name or their surname.

candidates.statement: The layout works on a phone and on a 14-inch laptop, but when the Slack browser window is shrunk for side-by-side use, navigating the application is hard, which is an area of improvement that could be considered.
context: Several windows open side by side

evidence_candidates.quote: when I minimize, not minimize, shrink the size of slack browser window, I feel like it's a little hard to navigate through the application.
I feel like that is an area of improvement that could be considered.

candidates.statement: Personal habit of keeping multiple windows open at the same time, with about three windows side by side.

evidence_candidates.quote: I tend to have multiple windows open at the same time.
So yeah, when I have and I have them side by side, so I would have like three windows open.
